evidence.note: Opens app structure, test runner, and app-basic contract/shim files before writing any code, establishing the fixture contracts as the source of truth.
Systematically maps the vendored plugin-rsc API: reads runtime API typedefs, RscPluginOptions type, README, and examples to understand the Vite/RSC plugin lifecycle it must build on.
Re-reads shims contracts, plugin-rsc runtime typedefs, react rsc/browser typedefs, and both app- and pages-router next-shims.d.ts, extracting precise type signatures for each subsystem being built.
Consults source for non-obvious semantics — RSC flight inlining, the browser callServer action-serialization convention, and next/cache usages — rather than guessing.
Greps fixtures for actual next/* imports and default exports, grounding shims in what the fixtures require rather than full Next.js behavior.
When NextRequest subclassing breaks, dives into undici Request source to resolve the edge case from source rather than guessing — targeted re-consultation mid-build.
Later stretch is dominated by npm offline-cache/install infrastructure debugging, not framework contract research, so semantic reference mining tapers.

reasoning: The agent systematically maps the Vite/plugin-rsc hooks and the vendored typedefs to each subsystem, extracts contracts from the fixture shims, grounds shims in actual fixture usage, and re-consults upstream source (flight inlining, callServer, react-dom edge, undici Request) when behavior is ambiguous rather than guessing — matching the level-8 anchor. It falls short of 10 because the sustained research is partly displaced in the back half by npm-infrastructure firefighting, and there is no visible written interlocking model of routing/RSC/resolution.
